comment: Rules of the new game (ADR 0028, docs/projekt-gry.md). Time: 10 ticks a second; rates are per minute of play. Amounts are whole units (two decimals allowed). density: how many times more hexes than the legacy map of the same size (a hex is room for one building). economyEveryTicks, populationEveryTicks: rhythms of docs/wydajnosc.md. Start: the stock and people of a new tribe. Food: every person eats foodPerPersonPerMinute; idle people forage idleForagePerMinute each. Growth: a fed settlement below its housing grows growthPercentPerMinute of its people a minute (at least minGrowthPerMinute); without food it loses starvePercentPerMinute. resumeCostPercent: resuming a paused construction costs this much of the building's price again. Settlement levels: radius in hexes of the territory, housing and storage given by the settlement itself, the price of the upgrade. Buildings: workers (jobs), price, buildSeconds, terrain rules (biomes, relief, needsWater = next to a lake, sea or river, deposit = a surface deposit on the hex, minFertility), production per worker per minute, deposit bonus in percent, housing and storage they add. bonusRelief and bonusReliefPercent: extra production on hills or mountains. Storage: goods lie in the settlement where they were made; every finished building adds buildingStorage of room for each good unless it gives its own storage (storehouses). Construction materials are carried by porters from the nearest storehouse (or the settlement centre) and the building time starts when they arrive. groups: tags that technology effects can aim at (e.g. melee, tools). foundSettlement.comment: Settlers found a camp at least minDistance hexes from every other settlement centre, on land nobody owns; their people live there.

terrainCost.comment: Walking cost of a hex in percent of a flat open hex.

research.comment: A technology needs experience in the technologies before it (worker-minutes in their buildings), then its price in goods and its time. It is cheaper by neighbourDiscountPercent for every known people that knows it (at most maxNeighbourDiscountPercent). One research at a time.

technologies.name: Foraging
technologies.gives: Gatherers, woodcutters, huts, storehouses, scouts, settlers, warriors.

technologies.name: Shelters
technologies.gives: Huts give 4 more homes; clay pits.

technologies.name: Sewing
technologies.gives: Tailors (clothing); hard winters half as harsh.

technologies.name: Rafts
technologies.gives: Raft landings; units cross rivers faster.

technologies.name: Masonry
technologies.gives: Stone houses, masons; villages can become towns.

technologies.name: Barter
technologies.gives: Trading posts; trade agreements and caravans to other peoples.

technologies.name: Bronze working
technologies.gives: Tin mines, bronze smiths, armourers (arms), spearmen.

technologies.name: The wheel
technologies.gives: Cartwrights, chariots; porters and caravans 50% faster.

technologies.name: Currency
technologies.gives: Markets; barter at fair worth; research −5%.

technologies.name: Construction
technologies.gives: Great storehouses; towns can become cities.

technologies.name: Roads
technologies.gives: Roads: walking on them twice as fast.

technologies.name: Medicine
technologies.gives: Bathhouses; growth +2% a minute; epidemics 30% milder.

thinkers.comment: A people has one thinker. Rarity sets how much cheaper (costPercent) and how much less experience (experiencePercent) research needs; some take less experience but cost more. A thinker retires after retireMinutes; the successor (II, III…) keeps the school but each generation loses generationLossPercent of the edge. A new candidate shows up every offerMinutes; hiring costs hirePrice times the rarity's priceTimes.

advisors.comment: A people has at most one advisor. A candidate shows up every offerMinutes with one or two fields (economy, growth, research, expansion); hiring costs hirePrice times the rarity's priceTimes, and the advisor eats upkeepFoodPerMinute. The advisor gives one piece of advice at a time, only in its fields.

war.comment: Units fight once a second (combatEveryTicks). A side deals people × strength × (100 + terrain bonus + upgrades) / 100 × luck (lowLuckPercent..highLuckPercent) hundredths of a person, killed on the other side. Melee reaches the next hex, ranged units their range. A settlement under attack defends with defenderPercent of its people at defenderStrength each, raised by its finished fortifications; at captureBelowPeople it is taken. Soldiers eat soldierFoodPerMinute each. Attacking a people without a declared war is a surprise attack: the victim and everyone who met both remember it (reputation).

events.comment: Every people draws one event from the shared pool every everyMinutes (a random minute within the spread), never one another people has right now. An event lasts its seconds. productionPercent changes the production of the listed goods, eatPercent what people eat, losePercentPerMinute kills that share of people a minute, destroyBuilding burns one random finished building at the start. field: the advisor field that gives advice on it.

pool.name: Drought
pool.advice: Drought: build fishing huts or stop growing for a while; the stores must last.

pool.name: Hard winter
pool.advice: A hard winter: people eat more. Keep food stores high and do not train settlers now.

pool.name: Epidemic
pool.advice: Sickness spreads: the fewer people we move around, the better; wait it out.

pool.name: Fire
pool.advice: A fire took a building: rebuild what we need most first.

pool.name: Flood
pool.advice: The rivers flood: fields and clay pits work at half. Use the stores.

diplomacy.comment: Peoples consider a treaty only when they have known each other for knownMinutes, their settlements are at most borderHexes apart, they have not fought for peaceMinutes and the other's reputation is above minReputation; then a trade agreement when they lack a good the other makes or the other knows more technologies, an alliance when they share an enemy. At most one offer to the same people every offerCooldownMinutes, refusalCooldownMinutes after a refusal. Trade agreements need the barter technology. Barter goods travel in caravans; the AI takes a barter worth acceptWorthPercent of what it gives (100 with currency) and keeps twice what it gives.
